Inadequate emergency management, treatment that does not do justice to a defenseless creature. I had reported the critical condition of a neighborhood cat I regularly cared for: the animal was in obvious distress, breathing very laboredly and unable to move or react.
Aware of the gravity of the situation and lacking the appropriate technical resources, we avoided any manipulation to avoid causing further trauma, trusting in the intervention of qualified personnel, remaining on site to await their intervention with the cat. Despite repeated reminders given the gravity of the situation, the rescuers arrived after hours of waiting.
​When the cat was picked up, despite being a defenseless, extremely docile, and completely debilitated animal, it was removed in an extremely abrupt and inappropriate manner, PULLED and LIFTED BY THE TAIL and placed inside the carrier, holding it upright, suspended by the tail.
It should be known that subjecting a cat's tail to traction can cause excruciating pain and serious damage. I immediately expressed my concerns. The staff responded by dismissing my concerns, saying that this is normal for street cats. While subjected to this forced traction, the animal complained, further aggravating an already critical health situation with this severe stress and unnecessary suffering.
​Later, after pressing for information, we were informed that the animal had already arrived at the emergency room deceased. This was disappointing, superficial, and lacking the respect due to a living being.
Very helpful and very professional staff

The facility and staff were efficient and courteous. They immediately responded to our request for help for an injured bird, despite it being the 15th of August.

Shameful and inhumane. Total disregard. I've twice reported a stray cat near death, mauled by a dog and infested with parasites. The response? "Call us when you've caught it, we're available 24/7. We're busy right now." They demand that a private citizen catch an injured and infected animal, ignoring the health risks for those who have other pets at home. Zero empathy, zero professionalism, and a complete failure to provide assistance. A facility like this is nothing short of a disgrace to animal welfare. Stay away.

I only had to complete administrative tasks. The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. The facility was easy to reach (by car) and very clean.

What I experienced with the Frullone Veterinary ASL was unacceptable.
Bringing a cat to an emergency and being met with a wall of silence, disorganization, and a complete lack of communication is something that should never happen in any public facility.

The office's behavior was irresponsible:

No information on the status of the cat brought in for emergency care.

No updates, no explanations, no human contact.

The public hotline on Wednesdays was deactivated, making it impossible to speak to anyone.

Every attempt to obtain information was futile, as if the citizen had no right to know what was happening.

The end result was the worst possible outcome: the cat died, and no one had the decency to report anything, either before or afterward.
A level of management that can only be described as "shameful."

A public facility that should guarantee transparency, care, and respect has instead proven closed, absent, and totally indifferent.
An experience that leaves me bitter and angry, and one I would not wish upon anyone.

When I first registered my cat colony, a relationship of trust had been established between me and them. They were kind and helpful. I brought my cat in for sterilization and picked her up that same day.
A male cat brought to the emergency room for a suspected infection was microchipped and neutered (without my order, but since he was a colony cat, they could have done it). They called me and I went to pick him up.
On February 27, 2026, I brought my cat back for treatment for a cold. The doctor on duty at the time, and the famous doctor, told me that my cat would not be returned to me because he is a colony cat. At most, I could go there to witness his release, but they wouldn't give him to me in his cage. 🤔
I point out to the doctor that they haven't behaved like this in the past, I was called, and I went to get him, the doctor's response:
I'm going to tell you that I'm going to give you a break!

I find myself writing this review months later, trying to calm my initial anger.

We found a kitten of about a month and a half in terrible condition. After lovingly caring for him at home for a week, we were forced to take him to the Frullone veterinary hospital for the necessary medical care, without imagining what would happen. The little one had a serious eye problem: he started out with conjunctivitis, but it turned out that one eye was affected by the herpes virus, so much so that it bulged out and had to be removed to avoid infection. The other eye, however, had very faint reflexes, and we hoped he might regain at least some vision, albeit blurry. From there, the nightmare began. For 10 days, I received no news, despite constant calls from me and the vet who had helped me.
No one knew where the kitten was; he wasn't even listed in the records. I was told he'd had eye surgery a week after being brought to the facility and that he'd been handed over to a caretaker, despite it being clear he should be returned to me, the person who'd found him. When they finally told me he'd be coming home, they didn't bring him back in time, saying "the cat wasn't ready" and that there were technical problems. After INSISTING so much to get him back, a guy who "delivers" animals to the local health authority put up with my constant calls and assured me that he'd bring him to me personally. I thank him again for his kindness. Unfortunately, once he got home, the cat had seizures, vomiting, and diarrhea. We did everything we could to treat him, but he didn't make it... it was clear he was born unlucky, but before leaving, the cat was fine, super active, playing, and eating.

A surreal experience, handled with disorganization, a lack of transparency, and respect, both for the animal and for the person who rescued him.

Could it have gone differently? We'll never know, but trust other facilities, where they keep you updated on your pet's condition and don't hear them say, "We can't find it in the register," over the phone (while talking to each other).
